analyst_view.overall: Early view: Juventus host Udinese four days before a Europa League trip to Hapoel Be'er Sheva, which is being played in Bucharest. Spalletti has a long injury list (Yildiz, Cambiaso, Nico Gonzalez, Locatelli, Khephren Thuram and Grabara missed the last game) and has complained about the team's inconsistency. Udinese are bottom and, according to Tuttomercatoweb, now coached by Paolo Zanetti after Runjaic left.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Juventus's home games have averaged only 2.2 goals, but Udinese concede 2.2 a game away, so the factors cancel out. Udinese's Davis had not scored a league goal before the break.

corners.text: The site expects 10.5 corners. I lean higher: Juventus win about 8.5 corners a game, the most in Serie A, and their home games have averaged close to 12. Udinese should defend deep and give away plenty.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. I lean slightly lower because Udinese's away games have averaged under two cards, the calmest of any team on the road along with Parma and Cagliari. Juventus rarely get booked at home.

shots.text: The site expects 29.5 shots. I lean lower, because Juventus's home games have averaged only about 22 shots: they control the ball but create little, and opponents take only seven shots a game in Turin. A rotated side before Europe adds to that.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean lower: Juventus's home games have averaged about 6.4 on target, the fewest at home of any of the top-seven sides. Udinese's away games are higher, but most of that comes from home sides shooting at them, and Juventus have not been doing much of that.
